recommendations.recommendation: Aspirin is recommended for all patients without contraindications at an initial oral LD of 150–300 mg (or 75–250 mg i.v.) and an MD of 75–100 mg o.d. for long-term treatment.
In all ACS patients, a P2Y12 receptor inhibitor is recommended in addition to aspirin, given as an initial oral LD followed by an MD for 12 months unless there is HBR.
A proton pump inhibitor in combination with DAPT is recommended in patients at high risk of gastrointestinal bleeding.
Prasugrel is recommended in P2Y12 receptor inhibitor–naïve patients proceeding to PCI (60 mg LD, 10 mg o.d. MD; 5 mg o.d. MD for patients aged ≥75 years or with a body weight <60 kg).
Ticagrelor is recommended irrespective of the treatment strategy (invasive or conservative) (180 mg LD, 90 mg b.i.d. MD).
Clopidogrel (300–600 mg LD, 75 mg o.d. MD) is recommended when prasugrel or ticagrelor are not available, cannot be tolerated, or are contraindicated.
If patients presenting with ACS stop DAPT to undergo CABG, it is recommended they resume DAPT after surgery for at least 12 months.
Prasugrel should be considered in preference to ticagrelor for ACS patients who proceed to PCI.
GP IIb/IIIa receptor antagonists should be considered if there is evidence of no-reflow or a thrombotic complication during PCI.
In P2Y12 receptor inhibitor–naïve patients undergoing PCI, cangrelor may be considered.
In older ACS patients, especially if HBR, clopidogrel as the P2Y12 receptor inhibitor may be considered.

Associated Conditions: Acute coronary syndrome (ACS) — target of P2Y12 receptor inhibitors (adjunct to aspirin, used around PCI and for long-term DAPT)
genes.context: Multiple recommendations reference the P2Y12 receptor inhibitor (recommended in all ACS patients in addition to aspirin; prasugrel recommended in P2Y12 inhibitor–naïve patients proceeding to PCI; cangrelor may be considered in P2Y12 inhibitor–naïve patients; clopidogrel as the P2Y12 receptor inhibitor may be considered in older/HBR patients).

Associated Conditions: Thrombotic complications/no-reflow during PCI — component of the platelet GP IIb/IIIa receptor complex targeted by GP IIb/IIIa receptor antagonists
genes.context: The guideline states GP IIb/IIIa receptor antagonists should be considered if there is evidence of no-reflow or a thrombotic complication during PCI (GP IIb corresponds to integrin alpha IIb, encoded by ITGA2B).
